title: QBR - Equinox Systems Health Check
header:
Date: 2026-11-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE); Dana Carter (Equinox VP ML), Luis Moreno (Infra Lead), Aisha Khan (Product), Ben Ortiz (Security), Claire Parker (Finance)
summary: Quarterly business review focusing on usage trends, cost variance, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment for Equinox's LLM features. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, upcoming 2.0 model rollouts, security/compliance ask list, and pilot metrics for caching and batching optimizations.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining our QBR, appreciate you making time. We'll run for about 45 minutes, go over usage, cost, reliability, and roadmap alignment. Priya and Marco are here to help with CS and technical questions.
[00:18] Dana Carter: Thanks Jordan. Just to set context, we've got the pair of product launches this quarter, feature A rolled out to 10% and feature B internal. We saw traffic bump in Oct. Curious about cost impact and latency spikes we hit mid-Oct.
[00:32] Priya Shah: Yep, we pulled the usage and cost dashboards ahead of this. We'll walk through numbers and then Marco will talk about the mid-Oct incident and what we've changed.
[00:44] Marco Ruiz: Quick note - transcript may have some ASR noise, but I'll try to be clear. So on Oct 18 we saw a KV cache miss storm on the canopy route which increased token compute by about 32% for 3 hours. That was due to a key eviction pattern when sequence lengths spiked. We deployed a cache warm policy and tuned batching windows; latency back to target within 40 minutes.
[01:10] Luis Moreno: Can you quantify the cost hit? Finance wants a number for the Oct spike.
[01:18] Priya Shah: For the Oct 18 incident, estimated incremental spend was ~$8.2k. Overall monthly spend for Oct was $112k, so the incident drove roughly a 7% bump that month.
[01:30] Claire Parker: OK that's helpful. We're still above forecast; what's driving the baseline increase month over month?
[01:38] Jordan Lee: Two main drivers - higher per-user prompt length from feature A and increased concurrent sessions. Also some routes moved to a higher-priority model variant which increases per-token cost. We recommended a rollout plan to move cold traffic to a quantized variant and keep hot paths on the non-quantized model.
[01:56] Aisha Khan: Remind me of the quality delta with quantized variants? We can't degrade customer-facing output.
[02:03] Marco Ruiz: In our evaluations the 4-bit quantized variant (Q4) had mean ROUGE/QA pass delta of under 1.5% on your eval sets for route X, and latency improved by ~18% on average. For safety-critical flows we recommend A/B testing before full swap.
[02:22] Dana Carter: Sounds reasonable. Can Redwood run a pilot for the quantized model on 5% of production?
[02:28] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. We'll scope a pilot: implement canary on the route, capture eval metrics and user-visible quality. We'll also capture cost delta.
[02:36] Ben Ortiz: Security checklist - we need confirmation on KMS integration, key rotation policy, SSO SAML flows, and audit log retention. Any changes on those since last quarter?
[02:47] Priya Shah: No breaking changes. For Private deployments you control the KMS; for Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS via our connectors and support rotation schedules. We can share the SOC2 Type II report and the KMS integration doc after the call.
[02:59] Ben Ortiz: Great. Also, audit log retention - what's the maximum retention for the hosted offering? We may need 1 year for compliance.
[03:07] Priya Shah: Hosted default is 90 days, but we have an add-on for extended retention up to 13 months. We'll include pricing in the follow-up.
[03:15] Claire Parker: On SLAs, are we still within the 99.9% target for the last quarter?
[03:21] Marco Ruiz: Yes - platform health metrics show 99.92% availability for your account region over the quarter. The Oct incident affected latency but not the overall availability SLA.
[03:31] Dana Carter: Looking ahead, we plan to double active users by end of Q1. We need guidance on capacity and whether to move to Dedicated.
[03:39] Jordan Lee: For scale of that size, Dedicated makes sense if you want predictable throughput and lower unit cost at steady state. We modeled two options: keep Hosted and leverage Reserved Bursts vs move to Dedicated with a 3-month ramp. We shared a cost model; Marco can walk the numbers.
[03:56] Marco Ruiz: Quick numbers: based on your projected 2x traffic and current route mix, Hosted projected monthly cost ~ $210k with additional burst plan. Dedicated with a small committed pool reduces per-token cost by ~27% and improves tail latency. Initial commit is typically month-to-month for early ramp, then quarterly.
[04:15] Luis Moreno: What's the procurement lead time for Dedicated? We need to engage infra procurement.
[04:21] Jordan Lee: Typical lead time is 4-6 weeks for a Dedicated deployment including capacity provisioning and network setup, shorter if you already have a private VPC connection.
[04:31] Aisha Khan: Any integration work on our side for dedicated? e.g., model pinning, rollouts?
[04:36] Marco Ruiz: Minimal - API remains the same. You'll have a control plane for pinning model versions and rollout rules. For private deployments we add a small agent for metrics and logging. We provide a runbook.
[04:47] Claire Parker: On billing, how do reserved capacity contracts work? We'll need clear monthly invoicing vs usage-based overages.
[04:55] Priya Shah: Reserved capacity is a commit with a monthly fee and defined throughput. Overages are billed at a pre-agreed rate. We'll provide a sample contract and an invoice mockup for your finance team.
[05:05] Dana Carter: Can we also get latency percentiles per route? We need p50/p95/p99 broken down by model variant.
[05:12] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can export that. Priya will share a latency dashboard with per-route percentiles and token-level cost breakdown.
[05:20] Priya Shah: Noted. We'll include p50/p95/p99, and separate by model variant and region.
[05:26] Luis Moreno: A technical question - how does Redwood handle cold starts on long sequences? We saw a p99 spike when a long sequence came in.
[05:34] Marco Ruiz: Longer sequences increase KV cache pressure and memory churn. We recommend a prefix caching strategy and sequence bucketing; we've also released a new kernel selection tweak that helps pre-allocate KV ranges. We can run a short benchmark against your sequence distribution.
[05:50] Dana Carter: Please do. That benchmark will inform whether we need more memory or change batching policies.
[05:56] Marco Ruiz: We'll need a 48-hour window of anonymized request traces (token lengths and route IDs) to run a representative benchmark. We'll redact any PII.
[06:05] Dana Carter: OK, I'll have Luis coordinate to share logs with your SE.
[06:10] Ben Ortiz: On compliance, we'll need the SOC2 report and the encryption in transit and at rest details, plus the KMS audit. Also curious about data residency options for our EU customers.
[06:20] Priya Shah: We have EU regions with data residency options. For Private deployments we can ensure all data stays in your VPC. We'll attach the security pack.
[06:28] Claire Parker: Roadmap - you mentioned a 2.0 model coming next quarter. How disruptive will that be to our pinned versions?
[06:35] Jordan Lee: Model 2.0 is a drop-in replacement in API terms, but we recommend staged rollouts. We'll expose a new model tag and rollout tools for canarying at 1%, 5%, 25% increments and rollback hooks. No code changes required unless you want to pin.
[06:51] Aisha Khan: Could Redwood run a fidelity test suite for our top 20 prompts once 2.0 is available?
[06:57] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we can run a fidelity/eval suite against a seeded prompt set and return pass/fail metrics and confidence intervals.
[07:05] Dana Carter: Great. Let's talk about next steps and who owns what.
[07:09] Jordan Lee: I'll summarize - action items and owners. Priya, can you capture commitments?
[07:14] Priya Shah: Yep. I'll list them in the QBR follow-up.
[07:17] Jordan Lee: Action items: 1) Redwood to run quantized model pilot at 5% on route X and report quality and cost delta (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2026-11-29). 2) Run sequence distribution benchmark (owner: Marco Ruiz + Luis Moreno, due: 2026-11-24). 3) Share SOC2 report, KMS integration doc, and extended log retention pricing (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-11-18). 4) Provide dedicated capacity cost model and sample contract (owner: Jordan Lee, due: 2026-11-22). 5) Share latency p50/p95/p99 per route and model variant (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-11-19).
[08:05] Claire Parker: That timeline looks good. Finance will review the Dedicated model once we have the sample contract.
[08:10] Jordan Lee: Anything else?
[08:12] Aisha Khan: One small ask - can we add automated smoke tests pre-rollout? A canary that runs synthetic prompts and validates expected outputs?
[08:20] Marco Ruiz: We support synthetic canary checks; we can add a smoke test to the rollout pipeline and surface regressions in the console. We'll propose a sample smoke test suite.
[08:28] Dana Carter: Thanks all. If you can get the SOC2 and contract items this week that helps procurement.
[08:33] Jordan Lee: We'll prioritize. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the notes and schedule a dedicated SE deep dive for the benchmark next week.
[08:40] (meeting ends)
